label: 5th generation: excess on non-severe non-covered treatment
unit: % of the cost borne by the patient
appliesTo: Holders of 5th generation policies claiming non-severe non-covered treatment
why: The other half of the trade the 2026 reform makes: a lower premium against a much larger share of non-essential non-covered costs staying with the patient. Read next to the fourth generation's 30% on non-covered treatment, it is the clearest single indicator of which policy suits someone who uses repeated outpatient therapy — and of how much a cheaper premium is actually buying.

history.display: 50% inpatient; outpatient 50% or ₩50,000, whichever is greater
history.source: Financial Services Commission — 5th generation indemnity health insurance
history.note: For non-severe non-covered treatment. The outpatient rule means small claims can be met entirely by the patient, since the fixed floor applies where it exceeds the percentage. The fourth generation applies 20% on benefit-covered and 30% on non-covered treatment, which is the comparison worth making before switching.
